hypothesis: V3 Candidate Hypothesis 2: Weekend Gap Fade

round_1_fixed_24h_hold_fade.description: Fixed-hold fade trade: gap = Sunday reopen Open vs Friday Close (>40h timestamp gap, Friday pre-bar); fade direction = -sign(gap), unconditional; hold exactly 24h from reopen; all 4 instruments (EUR_USD, GBP_USD, USD_JPY, XAU_USD), H1.

primary_test.interpretation: no detectable reversion signal - statistically indistinguishable from 50%/no correlation

stability_by_year.interpretation: correlation sign flips from weakly negative (2020-2022) to significantly POSITIVE - the opposite direction - in 2023-2024; not a stable structural relationship

round_2_closure_tracking.description: Does the gap show a tendency to partially/fully close, and how fast? EUR_USD & GBP_USD only, H1. No minimum gap size. Closure fraction = 1-(Close(t)-Friday_Close)/(Reopen_Open-Friday_Close), tracked via bar Close, max 120h window. Compared against a pre-specified baseline: identical closure test applied to ordinary non-weekend H1 moves (every 20th bar, systematic subsample).
round_2_closure_tracking.interpretation_closure_rates: Closure rates are very high (92-97%) but statistically indistinguishable from the ordinary-move baseline at 25% and 50%, and significantly LOWER than baseline at 100% closure - real weekend gaps do not close more reliably than an arbitrary ordinary hourly move given the same 5-day window. High closure is a generic feature of price wandering relative to a small recent reference distance, not a weekend-specific mechanism.

time_to_closure.interpretation: closure typically happens within the first 1-2 hours after reopen - too fast to represent a tradeable multi-day drift-back opportunity, more consistent with same-session settling

round_2_closure_tracking.up_vs_down_gaps: no meaningful asymmetry - similar closure rates and negative realistic P&L in both directions

cost_adjusted_edge_combined.interpretation: raw (cost-free) edge is small and not statistically significant at any threshold; realistic spread cost (~0.065-0.074%/trade) is 3-4x the size of that already-insignificant raw edge and flips every threshold decisively negative

stability_by_year_50pct_threshold.interpretation: closure rate is stably high every year, but so is the baseline - stability of a non-effect, not of a genuine edge

verdict: REJECTED. Round 1 (fixed 24h-hold fade) found no detectable reversion signal (r=-0.005, p=0.885; reversion rate 50.64%, statistically indistinguishable from 50%) and an unstable, sign-flipping year-by-year correlation. Round 2 (closure-tracking, the more rigorous test) found that real weekend gaps DO close at a high rate (92-97%) but at a rate statistically indistinguishable from - and at full closure, significantly lower than - an ordinary non-weekend-move baseline over the same 5-day window, meaning high closure is a generic feature of price wandering, not evidence of a weekend-specific mechanism. Closure also happens too fast (median 0-2h) to represent a tradeable multi-day opportunity. The raw cost-free edge was not statistically significant at any closure threshold in either round, and realistic transaction costs turn every measured edge decisively negative.
does_not_proceed_to: V3 build - hypothesis rejected at the cheap-falsification stage, before any strategy/entry-exit code was written.
